quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit, but be careful.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery roads. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: Signs placed everywhere there is danger.
Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
Diamond-shaped signs that are yellow or green.
Signs that warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white backgrounds. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing zones, turn restrictions, and other driving rules.

questions.question: You should never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When can you drive around railroad crossing gates?
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagging person, or a train's horn. Never try to drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop to look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must yield to other cars and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: The most common mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car.
questions.explanation: The most common backing mistake is not looking both ways behind the car. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Highway signs that show dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about hazards ahead. Follow these signs to stay safe. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.explanation: Stop signs are shaped like octagons (eight-sided signs). This shape is used only for stop signs. It tells drivers to stop completely before moving forward.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams turned on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view of the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. The number shown is the fastest legal speed you can drive. In bad weather or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: If a vehicle skids on water, the driver should quickly apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids on water, do not brake suddenly. Instead, release the gas and try to regain control. Let the skid pass on its own.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.
One driver should continue driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Then use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol affects driving.
The same way amphetamines affect driving.
The same way anger affects driving.
The same way driving with teenagers affects driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol affects driving.
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep and alcohol have similar effects on driving safety. Being awake for 18 hours affects you like having a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours affects you like having a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up above traffic speed to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs or other roadside objects.

questions.question: What do larger vehicles have?

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas near the rear that you cannot see in the mirrors.
